paragraphs.text: Good afternoon, sisters and elders. I've enjoyed another great day of zone interviews. You look so good and you sound so positive. You're simply inspiring to me.

I was able to get out to Valenzuela this morning and up to Baliuag, Malolos and Balagtas this afternoon while I was doing interviews. It was great. I was dualy productive. Very happy about that, like being productive. But being able to see some of you in person is a real blessing. I look forward to the day, hopefully soon, when we are able to meet and learn again together and also able to get out there and do some tracting. I know that you're now really missing tracting. Can you imagine a month ago missing tracting? It's interesting how things can change our perspective, isn't it?

Well, this weekend is general conference. We are so blessed to have the smartphones. I think we've got missionaries all over the Philippines right now, breaking the 10th commandment of, thou shalt not covet. I think they might be coveting our smartphones. Probably not. Anyway, we've got them and we're excited to be able to literally watch conference live as it happens, or at least for some of the sessions.

I want you to plan on watching all the sessions this conference. You can watch all three Saturday sessions on your Sabbath and then watch the two Sunday sessions on Monday morning. If you get up early enough, you'll be able to watch that final session probably live. But here's the good news. It's going to be a feast for those who are ready. Ready? It means hungry and thirsting for knowledge and truth.

During the interview, some of you have asked me how to be successful in life. I gave you a short answer, but your questions prompted me to remember a story I heard many years ago that really helped me to understand and be motivated to do the things I needed to do so that I could achieve the goals I set for myself. Let me share that story with you.

One day, a young man went to the home of Socrates, the great Greek philosopher, and asked, "Sir, I have come to seek your wisdom. Will you help me?" Socrates looked at the boy and replied, "How can I be of assistance?" The boy responded, "I want to be a great success. Will you teach me all that I need to know so I can be a great success?" "Certainly my son," replied Socrates, "walk with me."

Socrates began to walk and headed towards the sea. Once on the sand, Socrates just kept walking straight into the water. The young man followed it. When both were chest deep in the ocean, Socrates quickly placed his hands on the young man's head and forced it underwater. After just a few seconds, the young man fought his way to the surface and began to gasp for air. Socrates released the boy's head, turned and walked away.

The young man was appalled. He was angry. He had traveled a great distance to meet with a scholar whom he admired and respected, and when he asked for his wisdom, all he did was put his head underwater. Never again, vowed the young man, would he seek the advice of Socrates.

However, time, as we know, he had a way of healing wounds and after a week went by, the young man thought maybe he did something to upset Socrates. So he went back to visit the scholar. Again, he beseeched Socrates to teach him all that he needed to know so that he could be a great success. Socrates smiled and once again agreed. He asked the young man, "follow me."

And again, they walked toward the ocean. Just like before, Socrates walked into the water and when the water was about chest high, Socrates grabbed the young man by his head and pushed it underwater. But this time, however, the young man was ready. And before going under, he took a big gulp of air and held his breath for almost 60 seconds before fighting his way to the surface. As he wiped the water from his eyes, he saw that Socrates was already walking back towards the shore.

Now the young man was really angry. He was livid. Twice he had approached Socrates with the knowledge he needed to become a great success. And twice, Socrates had taken him to the ocean and tried to drown him. Never ever again would he be insulted and humiliated like this.

Well, 30 days passed and the young man had time to think about it and reflect. He really did want to be a success. Socrates had the wisdom that he needed so he decided to go one final time to see the scholar. Upon arriving at Socrates' home, he wrapped on the door. When the great philosopher appeared, the young man said, "I hope you remember me." Socrates flashed a big smile and said, "I do. You're the young man who wants to be a great success." The young man once again asked Socrates, "will you please teach me all I need to know and all I need to do to learn to be a great success?"

Socrates nodded and said, "absolutely." And then he started walking toward the ocean with the young man following in step. This time, the young man was well prepared as soon as Socrates grabbed his head. He took a deep swallow of air. He relaxed and was able to hold his breath under water for almost two minutes. When he finally surfaced for air, Socrates had already walked away.

Furious, the young man ran after Socrates. When he was a few feet from Socrates, he shouted, "Socrates, why isn't every time I come to you and just ask for your help to gain the wisdom and knowledge on how to be a great success, all you do is take me out in the water and dunk my head?" Socrates turned around and faced the young man and said, "son, I have tried three times now to teach you the secret of being a great success. The secret is simple. When you want to succeed as much as you want to breathe, you will be a great success."

So my dear friends, elders and sisters, as you go into conference, build your desire to really learn what the Lord wants you to learn so that you can have that hunger for truth just like the young man had the hunger and desire for air. Knowing the truth will not only set you free as the scriptures tell us, but will also give you clarity and power in all aspects of your life.

When you hunger and thirst after the good things, you are naturally able to turn away from those less worthy things. If you want to learn how to overcome thoughts that are not worthy or negative, if you want to learn how to avoid temptations that drag you down, know this. You have to want something that's good. So much, so much, that turning away from that hunger for that good thing is inconceivable to you. You would never waste your time chasing something that wasn't good because you're so driven to go after the good things that you want.

As you go into conference with that mindset, you're going to find yourself receiving personal revelation, which is more powerful than all the words that we might hear spoken by others, even prophets, seers and revelators, because what the Spirit teaches you is directly for you. So listen to the words, but also listen to the Spirit. And if you really want it, you will get it.

One final note to tell you, the government has told us just today that everyone living on Luzon must wear a mask whenever he or she goes outside. So elders and sisters, please abide by this rule with exact obedience. It is for your safety and for the safety of others. If you don't have a mask, or if your mask getting old or something, I mean they can last a long time, but if you need a mask, let me know, we will get one to you.

Make the day be a great one. You got a lot of time left. You can go out and really help somebody feel hopeful and happy. And the best way to do that is to choose to be hopeful and happy yourself. God bless you. I look forward to talking to some more of you tomorrow.
